feed_summary: Why the controls on an AI agent have to live outside of it, and what a security operations team can implement and maintain those controls. The new privileged user in your environment Security teams spent two decades learning how to work with the people they trust most. Domain admins, DBAs, finance approvers and contractors with VPN access all get a mature playbook: verified identity, scoped access, logged activity and a fast way to revoke it all. Today, we’re navigating the same kind of access with regard to AI agents. They read our mailboxes, query our data lakes, open tickets, push code and increasingly, act on production systems. Unlike a new hire, an agent can’t be interviewed, background-checked or made to sign an acceptable-use policy. The industry has largely settled on one framing:
title: Your Next Insider Threat Won’t be Human: Securing AI Agents From the Outside in
